_comment: The retrieval contract cadre's store enforces, as cases rather than prose.
Extracted while Store.Search still exists, because the contract lives only
inside it: after the engine moves to recall there is no way to re-derive
these from anything but memory. Any implementation claiming to be a
governed retrieval interface must refuse every case here.
recall's own Search takes filters a caller may omit and spans all
namespaces by default. That is not a defect in recall -- it is a library
for retrieval, not for governed retrieval. This file is the difference.

cases.name: no query
cases.why: A retrieval with no question is not a retrieval; refusing it early keeps the audit row meaningful.

cases.name: no classification
cases.why: Classification is the access decision. Without it the store cannot know what the caller may see, and a default would be a policy nobody wrote.

cases.name: no embedding provider
cases.why: Refused rather than defaulted: the provider and model are recorded in the audit row, so a silent default would make retrievals unattributable.

cases.name: no source scope decision
cases.why: The central refusal. A caller must choose between naming sources and deliberately spanning all of them; silence would default to reading every project's corpus.

cases.name: both all-sources and filters
cases.why: Ambiguous rather than resolvable. Picking either interpretation would silently widen or narrow what the caller sees.

cases.name: blank source filter entry
cases.why: A blank entry is a scope nobody chose. Treating it as a wildcard or dropping it would both be guesses.

also_required: Every completed retrieval is recorded with the embedding provider, model and result count, plus the retrieving agent and task id from SearchOptions.
